es: Reconocer el significado de modismos frecuentes de emociones y dinero (under the weather, on cloud nine, break the bank, cost an arm and a leg) a partir del contexto y valorar qué actitud transmiten.

teaching.en: I'm a bit under the weather today: I caught a cold at the weekend, and I am so exhausted that I can hardly think.
teaching.es: Estoy un poco indispuesto hoy: me resfrié el fin de semana y estoy tan agotado que apenas puedo pensar.
teaching.explanationEs: Under the weather significa «un poco enfermo»; no habla del clima. Lo aclaran las pistas: a cold, exhausted.
segments: I'm a bit under the weather today: I caught a cold at
the weekend, and I am so exhausted that I can hardly think.
teaching.audioText: I'm a bit under the weather today: I caught a cold at the weekend, and I am so exhausted that I can hardly think.

teaching.en: Ana has been on cloud nine since she got the job, and she is so thrilled that she keeps hugging everybody she meets.
teaching.es: Ana está en el séptimo cielo desde que consiguió el trabajo, y está tan encantada que abraza a todo el que encuentra.
teaching.explanationEs: On cloud nine = muy feliz. Cuidado: «estar en las nubes» en español es estar distraído.
segments: Ana has been on cloud nine since she got the job, and
she is so thrilled that she keeps hugging everybody she meets.
teaching.audioText: Ana has been on cloud nine since she got the job, and she is so thrilled that she keeps hugging everybody she meets.

teaching.en: I often feel blue on gloomy days, when the sky stays grey for a week and the evenings seem to start at noon.
teaching.es: Suelo sentirme decaído los días sombríos, cuando el cielo sigue gris durante una semana y las tardes parecen empezar al mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: Feel blue = sentirse triste. En inglés el azul se asocia con la tristeza; gloomy describe un día o un ánimo oscuro.
segments: I often feel blue on gloomy days, when the sky stays grey
for a week and the evenings seem to start at noon.
teaching.audioText: I often feel blue on gloomy days, when the sky stays grey for a week and the evenings seem to start at noon.

teaching.en: I'm broke this month, but a cheap lunch won't break the bank, so let's eat out once before the end of the week.
teaching.es: Estoy sin dinero este mes, pero un almuerzo barato no nos arruinará, así que comamos fuera una vez antes de que acabe la semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Break the bank = gastar tanto que te quedas sin dinero; se oye mucho en negativa (won't break the bank).
segments: I'm broke this month, but a cheap lunch won't break the bank,
so let's eat out once before the end of the week.
teaching.audioText: I'm broke this month, but a cheap lunch won't break the bank, so let's eat out once before the end of the week.

teaching.en: A new guitar can be costly: the one Tom wants could cost an arm and a leg, and he has not even played it yet.
teaching.es: Una guitarra nueva puede ser costosa: la que quiere Tom podría costar un ojo de la cara, y ni siquiera la ha tocado todavía.
teaching.explanationEs: Cost an arm and a leg = costar muchísimo. La imagen en inglés es un brazo y una pierna.
segments: A new guitar can be costly: the one Tom wants could cost an
arm and a leg, and he has not even played it yet.
teaching.audioText: A new guitar can be costly: the one Tom wants could cost an arm and a leg, and he has not even played it yet.

teaching.en: Try to save for a rainy day, so that you are not broke when the car breaks down, and later you can splash out on a holiday.
teaching.es: Intenta ahorrar para los tiempos difíciles, para no quedarte sin dinero cuando se averíe el auto, y más adelante podrás derrochar en unas vacaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Save for a rainy day = guardar dinero para imprevistos; splash out = gastar con alegría, sin mirar el precio.
segments: Try to save for a rainy day, so that you are not broke when

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere decir Mia con «under the weather» en su mensaje?

choices.text: She is worried about the night's forecast.
She is too busy to leave her house tonight.
She is slightly ill and needs to rest.

feedback.es: El médico le ha dicho que descanse: under the weather es estar un poco enfermo, no una preocupación por el tiempo ni por la agenda.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que dice el médico: ¿de qué problema habla?

origin.text: Mia's message: 'I can't come tonight, sorry. I am a bit under the weather, and the doctor told me to rest. Please tell everybody that the concert will have to manage without me.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Ana consiguió el trabajo y desde entonces está en el séptimo cielo.»

answer.text: cloud

feedback.es: On cloud nine es el modismo de la felicidad total: la imagen es una nube y el número nueve.

hint.es: Es un modismo de felicidad que aparece en la tabla de la clase: una nube.

origin.text: Ana got the job she had always dreamed about, and she has been on ___ nine ever since; even her friends say that they have never seen her so thrilled.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige por qué se sentía decaído el primo.

choices.text: Because an expensive guitar left him without money.
Because he had lost his guitar on the way home.
Because he was ill after a long weekend away.

feedback.es: Feel blue explica su ánimo y cost an arm and a leg junto con broke muestran la causa: el gasto en la guitarra lo dejó sin dinero.

origin.audio: My cousin called me on Sunday. He sounded gloomy, so I asked him what was wrong. He said he felt blue because he had spent too much on a guitar. It had cost an arm and a leg, and now he was broke until the end of the month. I told him to save for a rainy day next time.

pairs.es: sentirse triste sin un motivo claro
estar felicísimo por una buena noticia

feedback.es: Feel blue expresa tristeza, on cloud nine alegría, save for a rainy day previsión y break the bank un gasto excesivo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere decir «break the bank» en el mensaje de Sara?

choices.text: It will leave us without money for the month.
It will not cost more than we can afford.
It will be cheaper than cooking at home.

feedback.es: Won't break the bank significa que no será un gasto excesivo; Sara no compara con cocinar en casa ni anuncia que se quedarán sin dinero.

origin.text: Sara's message: 'Don't worry about the restaurant, it is cheap. A simple dinner for four won't break the bank, and afterwards we can walk by the river if the weather stays dry.'

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué actitud muestra Leo al final de la conversación.

choices.text: He is angry with the narrator for calling him.
He is happy because he has earned extra money.
He jokes about his situation, although he feels low.

feedback.es: Bromea sobre que no gastó nada y sobre el «rainy day», pero antes se describe cansado y sombrío: hace humor aunque está decaído.

origin.audio: Last Saturday I was supposed to meet my friend Leo at the cinema, but he never showed up. When I called him, he said he was under the weather and exhausted after a week of double shifts. He sounded gloomy, so I offered to bring him some soup. He laughed and said that, for once, his week had not cost an arm and a leg, because he had been too tired to spend any money. I told him to save for a rainy day, but he said that the rainy day had already arrived.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué Leo no gastó dinero esa semana.

choices.text: He was too tired to go out and spend.
He had decided to save for a rainy day.
He was waiting for his salary to arrive.

feedback.es: Leo explica que estaba demasiado cansado para gastar; la idea de ahorrar es un consejo de la narradora, no su razón.

feedback.es: Costly es el adjetivo formal para «que cuesta mucho»; expresa que la reparación superaba lo razonable.

origin.text: Repairing the old car would be far too ___, so Tom decided to sell it and take the bus to work until he could afford a cheaper one.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende la autora de esta columna sobre el dinero?

choices.text: Money is unimportant, because feelings have other causes.
Money is not everything, but it clearly affects our mood.
Money matters most, since it decides how we feel.

feedback.es: La autora matiza: rechaza que el dinero lo sea todo, pero reconoce que influye en el ánimo y que conviene ahorrar.

origin.text: People say that money cannot make you happy, yet when a friend is broke she is usually gloomy, and when she gets a raise she is on cloud nine. I do not believe that money is everything, but I admit that it helps to save for a rainy day.

prompt.es: ¿Qué deja entender Leo en su correo sobre la compra de las entradas?

choices.text: That he had planned the expense carefully months before.
That Mia had insisted that he should buy the tickets.
That he could not say no, although he now regrets the cost.

feedback.es: «I simply could not say no» muestra que compró por impulso, y «a little broke» que ahora lamenta el gasto.

origin.text: Hi Mia, sorry I missed the concert. I was under the weather all weekend, and to be honest I am a little broke after buying tickets that cost an arm and a leg. Next month I will save for a rainy day, but this time I simply could not say no.

That it is so high that the firm will struggle.

es: Adaptar tiempo, pronombre y posesivo en modismos flexibles (spill the beans, hit the roof, pull my leg) y reconocer los modismos fijos (once in a blue moon, out of the blue, by and large) que no admiten cambios.

vocabulary.en: let the cat out of the bag

teaching.en: Please don't spill the beans about the party, because the whole surprise depends on keeping it a secret until Saturday night.
teaching.es: Por favor, no reveles nada de la fiesta, porque toda la sorpresa depende de mantenerlo en secreto hasta el sábado por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Spill the beans es un modismo flexible: el verbo cambia de forma (spills, spilled, is spilling), el resto (the beans) no.
segments: Please don't spill the beans about the party, because the whole
surprise depends on keeping it a secret until Saturday night.
teaching.audioText: Please don't spill the beans about the party, because the whole surprise depends on keeping it a secret until Saturday night.

teaching.en: When Dad saw the broken window he hit the roof, and for ten minutes he was so furious that nobody dared to speak.
teaching.es: Cuando papá vio la ventana rota se puso furioso, y durante diez minutos estuvo tan furioso que nadie se atrevió a hablar.
teaching.explanationEs: El verbo del modismo va en pasado (hit); the roof se queda igual. Hit es igual en presente y pasado.
segments: When Dad saw the broken window he hit the roof, and for
ten minutes he was so furious that nobody dared to speak.
teaching.audioText: When Dad saw the broken window he hit the roof, and for ten minutes he was so furious that nobody dared to speak.

teaching.en: Are you trying to pull my leg? You must be joking, because nobody could finish that report in only one hour.
teaching.es: ¿Me estás tomando el pelo? Tienes que estar bromeando, porque nadie podría terminar ese informe en una sola hora.
teaching.explanationEs: El posesivo concuerda con la persona: pull my leg, pull your leg, pull his leg.
segments: Are you trying to pull my leg? You must be joking,
because nobody could finish that report in only one hour.
teaching.audioText: Are you trying to pull my leg? You must be joking, because nobody could finish that report in only one hour.

teaching.en: We eat out once in a blue moon, because we rarely have enough money or enough time to book a table.
teaching.es: Comemos fuera muy de vez en cuando, porque rara vez tenemos suficiente dinero o tiempo para reservar mesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Once in a blue moon es un modismo fijo: no admite cambios de palabras ni de orden. Rarely es su equivalente sencillo.
segments: We eat out once in a blue moon, because we rarely
have enough money or enough time to book a table.
teaching.audioText: We eat out once in a blue moon, because we rarely have enough money or enough time to book a table.

teaching.en: The offer came out of the blue, and it was so unexpected that Ana asked whether somebody was playing a joke on her.
teaching.es: La oferta llegó de repente, y fue tan inesperada que Ana preguntó si alguien le estaba haciendo una broma.
teaching.explanationEs: Out of the blue también es fijo: siempre con the y en singular.
segments: The offer came out of the blue, and it was so unexpected

teaching.audioText: The offer came out of the blue, and it was so unexpected that Ana asked whether somebody was playing a joke on her.

teaching.en: By and large, the team kept the secret well, but Tom let the cat out of the bag, and the surprise was gone.
teaching.es: En general, el equipo guardó bien el secreto, pero Tom se fue de la lengua y la sorpresa se acabó.
teaching.explanationEs: By and large es fija y suele ir al principio; let the cat out of the bag es flexible: Tom let, she lets, they have let.

the cat out of the bag, and the surprise was gone.

his father will hits the roof.

feedback.es: Después de will va el verbo base (hit) y el nombre del modismo no cambia (the roof).

hint.es: Tras will el verbo no se conjuga, y el sustantivo del modismo no va en plural.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Me estás tomando el pelo o hablas en serio?»

hint.es: Empieza con Are you pulling y termina con serious.

prompt.es: Según la nota, los modismos con verbo cambian de tiempo: ¿cuál es fija?

choices.text: spill the beans
once in a blue moon
pull my leg

feedback.es: Once in a blue moon no tiene verbo que conjugar ni palabra que cambiar; los otros dos modismos tienen un verbo flexible.

origin.text: Teacher's note: 'Idioms with a verb change tense: she spills, spilled or is spilling the beans. A few expressions, however, are frozen: they accept no tense, no plural and no other article, because every word stays exactly as it is.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi hermano siempre se pone furioso cuando pierde una partida.»

answer.text: hits

feedback.es: Con he/she/it en presente el verbo lleva -s: hits; the roof no cambia.

origin.text: My brother always ___ the roof when he loses a game, and my mother always tells him that it is only a game.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige cómo se estropeó la fiesta sorpresa.

choices.text: The best friend told the sister about the party on purpose.
The sister found the cake in the kitchen by accident.
The brother gave away the surprise in a chat with her friend.

feedback.es: El hermano mencionó el pastel de repente en una llamada con la mejor amiga de la hermana; no fue una traición deliberada ni un hallazgo casual.

origin.audio: My sister called me yesterday, and she was furious. She told me that our brother had spilled the beans about her surprise party. I asked whether she was pulling my leg, because he is usually very careful. She said no: he had mentioned the cake out of the blue during a phone call with her best friend. By and large she forgives him quickly, but this time she hit the roof.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué deja entender la hablante al preguntar «pulling my leg».

choices.text: That she finds the mistake surprising for a careful brother.
That she thinks her sister enjoys telling funny stories.
That she already knew about the party from the start.

feedback.es: Pregunta si es una broma porque el hermano suele ser muy cuidadoso: le sorprende que haya cometido ese error.

origin.audio: My sister called me yesterday, and she was furious. She told me that our brother had spilled the beans about her surprise party. prompt.es: Completa las tres frases adaptando cada modismo.

answer.text: hit | spill | pulls

feedback.es: El verbo cambia según la estructura (hit en pasado, don't spill tras el auxiliar, she pulls en presente) y el resto del modismo se conserva.

sentences: Last week my boss ___ the roof about the report, although he had read it only once.
Please don't ___ the beans about the gift, because my sister has not opened it yet.

origin.text: Traducción: «La semana pasada mi jefe se puso furioso por el informe.» «Por favor, no reveles nada del regalo.» «Ella siempre le toma el pelo con historias tontas.»

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina la guía de estilo de cambiar un modismo fijo?

choices.text: It is a fair way to avoid repeating the same idiom.
It makes the writer look careless rather than original.
It is fine as long as the meaning stays clear.

feedback.es: La guía dice que el escritor que cambia un modismo fijo «suena descuidado», no creativo; solo los flexibles admiten cambios.

origin.text: Style guide: 'Idioms add colour, but a few of them are frozen and must be copied exactly. Writers who change them to sound different, saying one time in a blue moon or out of a blue, do not sound creative; they sound careless. Flexible idioms, in contrast, allow new tenses and pronouns.'

title.es: Modismos en una charla de amigos
